articles.title: Terror attack on IAF station foiled: Gujarat ATS arrests JeM operative, rifle recovered
articles.description: Gujarat ATS thwarted a planned terrorist attack targeting a security establishment in the state. Officials arrested the suspect, Mohammad Islam Kabiruddin, who is linked to Jaish-e-Mohammed. During the arrest, authorities discovered an AK-47-style rifle, ammunition, and a Jaish-e-Mohammed flag in his possession. The perpetrator's handler provided financial support to facilitate his operations and escape.

articles.title: DMK 'ready' to back BJP's Delimitation Bill if TN's representation remains unchanged
articles.description: DMK has indicated their readiness to support the BJP's proposed delimitation bill with specific conditions. The party seeks to maintain Tamil Nadu's representation and ensure a freeze on new delimitation for 25 years. Recently, DMK communicated these demands to BJP, showing an openness to negotiation. Meanwhile, CPM expressed concern over this potential agreement and urged DMK to protect Tamil Nadu's interests.

articles.title: Stock market today: Sensex falls over 600 points, Nifty slips below 25,750 after 2-day rally
articles.full_text: Indian benchmark indices extended losses in afternoon trade on Friday, with the Sensex falling nearly 750 points and the Nifty slipping below the 25,700 mark. The BSE Sensex declined 749.09 points, or 0.89%, to 83,579.50, while the Nifty 50 dropped 208.55 points, or 0.81%, to 25,675.90 at 1:57 pm. Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty drifted lower in early trade after a two-day rally amid profit-taking in blue-chip IT stocks and HDFC Bank. From the Sensex pack, Tata Consultancy Services, HCL Tech, Infosys, HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries and Bajaj Finserv were among the major laggards. Titan, Tata Steel, Bharat Electronics and Power Grid were among the winners. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded at USD 96.50 per barrel. Rupee plunged 24 paise to 92.62 against the US dollar in early trade on Friday, dragged down by a recovery in crude oil prices and subdued sentiment in domestic equity markets. Sustained inflow of foreign funds and a softening dollar capped the fall in the Indian currency, forex traders said. In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 92.44 and declined to 92.62 against the greenback, trading 24 paise lower from its previous close. On Thursday, the rupee settled down 18 paise to 92.38 against the US dollar, a day after jumping 65 paise to reach its highest level this fiscal year so far. Indian equity benchmarks traded largely flat in early deals on Friday, with the Sensex and Nifty showing little movement. The BSE Sensex was trading at 84,237.51, down 91.08 points, or 0.11%, at 9:16 am. The Nifty 50 edged up 13.45 points, or 0.05%, to 25,897.95. Gift Nifty futures were at 25,962 points as of 7:51 am, indicating a positive start for the benchmark index. The Nifty had closed at 25,884.50 on Thursday. Indian shares are expected to open higher on Friday as they look to extend their winning run to a fifth straight week, with the unwinding of global AI trade driving a return of foreign flows into local stocks. GIFT Nifty futures were at 25,962 points, as of 7:51 am IST, indicating a positive start for the benchmark Nifty 50 index, which closed at 25,884.5 on Thursday, Reuters reported. The 50-stock index and the BSE Sensex are up 0.3% and 0.5%, respectively, so far this week, consolidating after a blistering surge of 14.2% and 14.8% over the last four weeks. Brent crude prices hovered near their monthly high on Friday as attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure raised concerns over oil supplies from the conflict-hit region. Brent crude futures fell 38 cents, or 0.39%, to $96.19 a barrel at 7.10am IST, after rising nearly $2 on Thursday to settle at their highest level since November 6. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures traded at $85.41 a barrel, up $1.73, or 2.07%, from Wednesday's close. There was no settlement on Thursday due to the Thanksgiving holiday. Asian markets were mostly higher in early trading on Friday, tracking developments in global markets after Wall Street remained closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.7% to 57,919.30, while Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.4% to 8,800.50. South Korea's Kospi surged 2.2% to 4,812.65. Hong Kong's Hang Seng edged up 0.4% to 22,310.11, while China's Shanghai Composite slipped 0.1% to 3,473.40. Stocks linked to artificial intelligence continued to attract buying, although profit-taking limited gains. In Japan, shares of Tokyo Electron and Advantest initially fell but quickly recovered, highlighting continued investor interest in semiconductor and AI-related stocks. Investors are also assessing the potential impact of planned US tariff hikes. US markets are scheduled to reopen later on Friday for a shortened trading session. The US dollar remained close to a 22-month high on Friday in thin holiday trading, with investors watching equity markets for clues amid growing concerns over the artificial intelligence (AI) trade and heightened volatility. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six major currencies, was steady at 103.81. It touched 104.53 on Monday, its highest level since March 2025, before giving up those gains the following day. The index is largely unchanged for the week. Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty rallied for the second day on Thursday amid investors' optimism over sustained foreign fund inflows and heavy buying in IT stocks. The 30-share BSE Sensex climbed 390.31 points, or 0.46 per cent, to settle at 84,328.59. During the day, it jumped 613.46 points, or 0.73 per cent, to 84,551.74. The 50-share NSE Nifty rose 65.25 points, or 0.25 per cent, to end at 25,884.50.

articles.title: Bihar designates five DIETs as regional language centres to promote Maithili, Bhojpuri, Magahi and other mother tongues in schools
articles.description: The Bihar government has designated five DIETs as regional language enrichment centres to promote Maithili, Magahi, Bhojpuri, Angika and Bajjika in school education. The centres will develop mother tongue-based learning resources, train teachers, document folk literature and conduct language research. The initiative, aligned with NEP 2020, also aims to preserve Bihar’s linguistic heritage and improve classroom learning.

articles.title: Agnipath scheme update: Up to 98% Agniveers may choose to continue in armed forces
articles.description: Around 80% of the Indian Army's first batch of Agniveers had expressed interest in continuing military service beyond four years, according to officials. Following the Centre's November 2026 changes to the Agnipath scheme, the estimated willingness to remain in the armed forces could rise to 97-98%. The revised arrangement offers the remaining 75% an additional two-year engagement, followed by an opportunity for regular enrolment subject to willingness and selection criteria.

articles.title: KSET 2026 revised provisional result released, check subject-wise cut-off marks and qualifying status
articles.description: The Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) has released the revised provisional KSET 2026 results and subject-wise cut-off marks for all 37 subjects. The revision follows a technical error in the allocation of SCC(MB) category slots in the earlier result. KEA has clarified that changes affect SCC(G) and SCC(MB) categories, while other categories remain unchanged. Of 1,29,214 registered candidates, 1,17,638 appeared for the examination conducted on October 11, 2026.

articles.title: ‘Star Trek' actor Jonathan Frakes shares his cancer diagnosis
articles.description: Jonathan Frakes faced a serious health scare just before a fan convention when he began noticing unusual symptoms, including pink urine. Concerned, he sought medical attention, which led to a cystoscopy diagnosis of bladder cancer. He promptly underwent surgery and chemotherapy, and now advocates for immediate medical evaluation for similar symptoms. His co-star Brent Spiner echoed this important message, emphasizing the critical nature of acting swiftly in health matters.
